note: Adjudicated variants: one of punctuation and one of orthography (the house i/j rule). Substantive text agrees across both witnesses with zero further divergence.

adjudicated.ruling: No comma before the apposition Dómini nostri Jesu Christi, with handmissal-eo and with the corpus ruling at ordinarium.suscipe-sancta-trinitas w016 for the same phrase. The typical edition prints the comma; the corpus keeps its own rule, and the reading is recorded here so the choice is visible.

The j-form against this edition's i-form, by the house rule in ORTHOGRAPHY.md. This edition prints i because the books it edits do: the 1962 typical edition sets Iesu, Ioánnem, iube and maiestátis throughout, and so does the Mszał Rzymski of the Tyniec Benedictines (Pallottinum, Poznań 1963), which is the book a Polish reader is most likely to hold. The mid-century hand missals print j; neither spelling is a different word, and the apparatus records theirs.
